52-61-53-820-801Forward Airstair Door Lock Mechanism Adjustment and TestPDF p. 1415

2. Forward Airstair Door Lock Mechanism Adjustment and Test (Figure 501)

A. General

(1) For the correct adjustment of the lockpin [1], it is necessary to get these clearances: (a) When the lockpin [1] is extended, the vertical clearance between the top of the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501). (b) When the lockpin [1] is retracted in the NORMAL and STANDBY modes, vertical clearance between the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501).

B. References

Reference Title 52-71-61-820-801 Forward Airstair Door Lockpin Sensor S282 Adjustment (P/B 201)

C. Consumable Materials

Reference Description Specification G01048 Lockwire - MS20995C32, Corrosion Resistant Steel - 0.032 Inch (0.8128 mm) Diameter NASM20995

D. Location Zones

Zone Area 117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left

E. Access Panels

Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door 117BL Forward Airstair Door

F. Prepare for the Adjustment

SUBTASK 52-61-53-860-025 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR A 17 C00246 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT NORMAL A 18 C00270 FWD AIRSTAIR TREAD LIGHT B 17 C00850 FWD AIRSTAIR ACTUATOR C 16 C01254 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT STBY C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 52-61-53-860-006 (2) Make sure this access panel is closed: Number Name/Location 117BL Forward Airstair Door is closed. SUBTASK 52-61-53-860-007 (3) Get access to the lockpin actuators [3] through this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door

G. Forward Airstair Door Lock Mechanism Adjustment

SUBTASK 52-61-53-820-001 (1) Adjust the lockpin [1] extended position: (a) If they are installed, remove the castelated nuts [7], cotter pins [8], washers [9], and bolts [10] that attach the normal system extension rod [2] and the standby system extension rod [4] to the rocker arm [5]. (b) Turn the normal system extension rod [2] and the standby system extension rod [4] until you get these conditions: 1) The vertical clearance between the top of the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501). NOTE: You must temporarily install the bolts through the extension rods and rocker arm to measure the vertical clearance. 2) The dimension between the bottom of the normal system extension rod [2] and the standby system extension rod [4] and the top of the actuators [3] is as shown (Figure 501). (c) Loosely install the washers [9], bolts [10], and castelated nuts [7] that connect the normal system extension rod [2] and the standby system extension rod [4] to the rocker arm [5]. (d) Make sure that the horizontal clearance between the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501). (e) Make sure the lockpin [1] height above the sill web is 0.085 in. (2.16 mm) - 1.150 in. (29.21 mm). NOTE: This is an approximate dimension and can change if the forward airstair door height changes. SUBTASK 52-61-53-860-026 (2) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR A 17 C00246 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT NORMAL A 18 C00270 FWD AIRSTAIR TREAD LIGHT B 17 C00850 FWD AIRSTAIR ACTUATOR C 16 C01254 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT STBY C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR SUBTASK 52-61-53-820-002 (3) Adjust the lockpin [1] retracted position: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Move the crossbolt [6] above the lockpin [1]: 1) Open the access door to get to the exterior control switches. 2) Move the exterior control to the NORMAL EXTEND position until the clearance between the outboard bottom edge of the airstair door and the outboard bottom edge of the door opening is 0.550 in. (13.97 mm) - 0.750 in. (19.05 mm). 3) Look through the door opening to make sure the crossbolt [6] is above the lockpin [1]. WARNING MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS NO POWER TO THE DOOR ACTUATOR MOTORS. THE DOOR ACTUATOR MOTORS CAN OPERATE IF THE POWER IS ON. IF THE DOOR ACTUATOR MOTORS OPERATE, INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (b) Remove power from the door actuator motors: 1) Disconnect the D912 and D914 electrical connectors from the door actuator motors. (c) Make sure the retracted lockpin [1] is in the correct position: NOTE: Two persons are necessary to do this task. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY POWER TO THE ACTUATORS FOR MORE THAN 120 SECONDS. WHEN YOU APPLY POWER TO THE ACTUATORS FOR MORE THAN 120 SECONDS, DAMAGE TO THE ACTUATORS CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY POWER TO THE ACTUATORS FOR MORE THAN 5 CYCLES, ONE AFTER THE OTHER ONE. SPECIFY A CYCLE BY A TIME OF POWER APPLIED TO THE ACTUATOR FOLLOWED BY AN EQUAL QUANTITY OF TIME WITH THE POWER OFF. IF POWER IS APPLIED TO THE ACTUATORS FOR MORE THAN 5 CYCLES, ONE AFTER THE OTHER ONE, DAMAGE TO THE ACTUATORS CAN OCCUR. 1) Move the exterior controls to the NORMAL EXTEND position to retract the lockpin [1]. a) While the lockpin [1] is retracted, make sure the vertical clearance between the lockpin [1] and crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501). b) Release the exterior control. 2) If it is necessary, turn the normal system extension rod [2] to get the correct clearance between the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6]. 3) Move the exterior controls to the STANDBY EXTEND position to retract the lockpin [1]. a) While the lockpin [1] is retracted, make sure the vertical clearance between the lockpin [1] and crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501). b) Release the exterior control. 4) If it is necessary, turn the standby system extension rod [4] to get the correct clearance between the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6]. 5) When the lockpin [1] is retracted with NORMAL power, make sure the clearance between the lockpin [1] and crossbolt [6] is correct. 6) Connect the D912 and D914 electrical connectors to the door actuator motors. EFFECTIVITY ALL 7) Use the exterior controls to open and close the forward airstair door. 8) Make sure the clearance between the top of the lockpin [1] and the crossbolt [6] is as shown (Figure 501). (d) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048, between the washers [11] and jamnuts [12] on the actuators [3]. (e) Install the cotter pins [8] in the castelated nuts [7] that connect the normal system extension rod [2] an the standby system extension rod [4] to the rocker arm [5]. SUBTASK 52-61-53-410-003 (4) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117A Electronic Equipment Access Door SUBTASK 52-61-53-820-004 (5) Do this task: Forward Airstair Door Lockpin Sensor S282 Adjustment, TASK 52-71-61-820-801. SUBTASK 52-61-53-710-003 (6) Do a test of the forward airstair lockpin mechanism: (a) Put the airstair controls in the NORMAL EXTEND position. 1) Make sure the airstair door opens. 2) Release the controls when the airstair door is fully open. (b) Put the airstair controls in the NORMAL RETRACT position until the airstair door is fully closed. (c) Put the airstair controls in the STANDBY EXTEND position. 1) Make sure the airstair door opens. 2) Release the controls when the airstair door is fully open. (d) Put the airstair controls in the STANDBY RETRACT position until the airstair door is fully closed.

E. Installation

SUBTASK 52-61-54-420-001 (1) Install the snubber as follows: EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Put the snubber on the splines at the end of the jackscrew shaft. Make sure the snubber face is away from the ball nut. (b) Put the jackscrew into the actuator. (c) Compress the snubber approximately 0.27 inch until the jackscrew gets to the bottom in the actuator. (d) Install the washer and locknut on the inboard end of the jackscrew. SUBTASK 52-61-54-860-005 (2) Release the forward airstair door from the closed position. SUBTASK 52-61-54-860-006 (3) Put the ballnut in position on the carriage. SUBTASK 52-61-54-420-002 (4) Install the two bushings to connect the ballnut to the carriage. SUBTASK 52-61-54-220-001 (5) Make sure the jackscrew turns freely as follows: (a) Do this task: Forward Airstair Door Actuator Standby System Motor Removal, TASK 52-61-59-000-801. (b) Turn the actuator manual drive to move the carriage along the rails. (c) Make sure the jackscrew turns freely. (d) If it is necessary, adjust the bottom guide fitting to correctly align the carriage with the guide rails. (e) Do this task: Forward Airstair Door Actuator Standby System Motor Installation, TASK 52-61-59-400-801.

Do only the steps to do an adjustment check of the forward door open limit switches. SUBTASK 52-61-54-710-001 (4) Operate the forward airstair door electrically. E. Prepare for the Adjustment

SUBTASK 52-61-60-860-004 (1) Make sure that these circuit breakers are open and have safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR A 17 C00246 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT NORMAL A 18 C00270 FWD AIRSTAIR TREAD LIGHT B 17 C00850 FWD AIRSTAIR ACTUATOR C 16 C01254 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT STBY C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR SUBTASK 52-61-60-860-005 (2) Make sure the forward airstair door is open: (a) Do this task: Forward Airstair Door Actuator Standby System Motor Removal, TASK 52-61-59-000-801. (b) Turn the actuator manual drive to open the forward airstair door.

F. Adjustment

SUBTASK 52-61-60-820-001 (1) Adjust the switch as follows: (a) Loosen the locknuts on the door closed switch. (b) Move the switch outboard as far as the threads permit and tighten the locknuts. (c) Apply clay, G02020 to the outboard face of the switch plate. NOTE: The clay, G02020 is used to make a mark to measure the clearance between the switch plunger and the switch plate. (d) Manually close this access panel as follows: Number Name/Location 117BL Forward Airstair Door 1) Turn the manual drive until the crosspin moves outboard of the latch pin or a person outside signals that the exterior of the door makes a continuous surface with the fuselage. (e) Make sure the stop pins touch the bearing plates. (f) Manually open the forward airstair door. (g) Find the clearance between the end of the switch plunger and the switch plate (door closed) as follows: 1) Measure the thickness of the clay, G02020 at the center of the mark in the clay. (h) Adjust the position of switch as follows: EFFECTIVITY ALL 1) Move the switch inboard by the amount of clearance measured from the mark in the clay, G02020 plus 0.07 to 0.11 inch (1.78-2.79 mm). (i) Clean the clay, G02020 from the switch plate. (j) Do this task: Forward Airstair Door Actuator Standby System Motor Installation, TASK 52-61-59-400-801. SUBTASK 52-61-60-860-006 (2) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR A 17 C00246 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT NORMAL A 18 C00270 FWD AIRSTAIR TREAD LIGHT B 17 C00850 FWD AIRSTAIR ACTUATOR C 16 C01254 FWD AIRSTAIR CONT STBY C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR SUBTASK 52-61-60-210-001 (3) Do a test of the switch: (a) Operate the forward airstair door: 1) If you replaced the S207 switch, make sure that you use the NORMAL mode to operate the door. If you replaced the S208 switch, make sure that you use the STANDBY mode to operate the door. 2) Make sure the switch operates correctly to stop the actuator. 3) Make sure the STAIRS IN OPERATION light at the internal control panel goes off when the door is closed. 4) Make sure the AIRSTAIR light at the Forward Overhead Panel, P5, is off when the door is closed. (b) Do a check of the forward airstair door: 1) With the door closed and the latch pin fully extended, make sure the inboard face of crosspin does not touch the outboard face of latch pin. 2) Open this access panel: Number Name/Location 117BL Forward Airstair Door 3) Apply clay, G02020 to all eight bearing plates around the door opening. 4) Close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117BL Forward Airstair Door electrically. 5) When the actuator stops, open the door and make sure all the stop pins touched the bearing plates. (c) If the airstair door does not fully close, do the steps as follows: 1) Adjust the position of the door closed switch outboard as necessary to get the forward airstair door to fully close. 2) Do a check of the forward airstair door again. EFFECTIVITY ALL (d) If the door is adjusted correctly, do the steps as follows: 1) Install MS20995C32 lockwire, G01048 on the locknuts which attach the switch to the switch bracket. 2) Clean the clay, G02020 from the bearing plates. 3) Fully close this access panel: Number Name/Location 117BL Forward Airstair Door

ATA 52-61-62

2 tasks
52-61-62-020-801Forward and Aft Rail RemovalPDF p. 1451

2. Forward and Aft Rail Removal (Figure 401)

A. References

Reference Title 52-61-00-860-801 Forward Airstair Extension (P/B 201)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left

C. Prepare for the Removal

SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-001 (1) Do this task: Forward Airstair Extension, TASK 52-61-00-860-801 to get access to the rail assembly.

D. Procedure

SUBTASK 52-61-62-010-001 (1) Open the airstair door to get access to the forward rail [1] and aft rail [2]. SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-002 (2) Remove the wire harness. (a) Disconnect the airstair electrical connector (P1) [15]. (b) Remove the speed-up limit switch, S13 [16] from the forward rail [1]. (c) Remove screws attaching the wire harness to the forward rail [1]. (d) Remove the channel [17] between the forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2]. (e) Attach the loose wire bundle and the channel [17] to the aft rail [2]. SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-003 (3) Remove the forward and aft rail bonding jumpers [3]. (a) Remove the bolts [4], washers [5], and nuts [6] from the bonding jumpers [3] on the forward rail [1] and aft rail [2]. (b) Keep the bonding jumpers [3] attached to the floor structure. Move the wires out of the way. SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-004 (4) Remove the sway braces [7] that are between the first and second rail attach fittings [14] from the floor structure. (a) Remove the bolts [8], washers [9], and nuts [10] from the airstair brackets. SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-005 (5) Remove the forward rail [1] from the floor structure. EFFECTIVITY ALL (a) Remove the shoulder bolts [11], washers [12], and nuts [13] from the rail attach fittings [14]. (b) Remove the forward rail [1] from the airstair opening. SUBTASK 52-61-62-020-006 (6) Remove the aft rail [2] from the floor structure. (a) Make sure that the swing arm assembly [18] is tied to the aft rail [2]. (b) Remove the shoulder bolts [11], washers [12], and nuts [13] from the rail attach fittings [14]. (c) Remove the aft rail [2] from the airstair opening.

52-61-62-400-801Forward and Aft Rail InstallationPDF p. 1452

3. Forward and Aft Rail Installation (Figure 401)

A. Tools/Equipment

NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional. Reference Description SPL-3937 Pin - Alignment, Bolt Installation Part #: ST9501B Supplier: 81205

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left

C. Procedure

SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-001 (1) Install the forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2] to the airplane floor structure inside the airstair door opening. (a) Install the alignment pins [19], (bolt installation alignment pin, SPL-3937) on the shoulder bolts [11]. (b) Install the shoulder bolts [11] through the rail attach fittings [14]. (c) Remove the alignment pins [19], (bolt installation alignment pin, SPL-3937) and install the washers [12] and nuts [13]. (d) Tighten the nuts between 100 in-lb (11.298 N·m) to 150 in-lb (16.948 N·m).. SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-002 (2) Install the sway braces [7] to the airstair brackets that are between the first and second rail attach fittings [14]. (a) Install the bolts [8], washers [9], and nuts [10] at two locations. SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-003 (3) Do a check of the spacing between the forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2]. (a) Measure the spacing between the forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2] at the first, third, and fifth attach fittings [14]. EFFECTIVITY ALL (b) If the measured dimension is more than the limits, the floor installation rail attach points must be rechecked. SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-004 (4) Install the bonding jumpers [3] between the floor structure, forward rail [1] and the aft rail [2]. (a) Install the bonding jumpers [3] adjacent to the outboard rail attach fittings [14]. (b) Install the bolt [4], two washers [5], and the nut [6] through the bonding jumper [3] lug into the forward rail [1] or the aft rail [2]. (c) Install the bolt [4], three washers [5], and the nut [6] through the bonding jumper [3] lug into the floor structure, if removed. SUBTASK 52-61-62-420-005 (5) Install the wire harness. (a) Install the channel [17] to the forward rail [1] and aft rail [2]. (b) Attach the wire bundle to the forward rail [1]. (c) Install the speed-up limit switch, S13 [16] to the forward rail [1]. (d) Connect the airstair electrical connector (P1) [15]. CAUTION MAKE SURE THAT THE CONDUIT SWING ARM BETWEEN THE AIRSTAIR CARRIAGE AND THE LADDER IS IN ITS CORRECT POSITION. IF IT IS INCORRECTLY ALIGNED , IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (e) Make sure that the swing arm conduit is correctly aligned.

52-71-00-730-801Door Warning System TestPDF p. 1477

2. Door Warning System Test (Figure 501)

A. Location Zones

Zone Area 211 Flight Compartment - Left 212 Flight Compartment - Right 821 Forward Cargo Door 822 Aft Cargo Door 830 Subzone - Passenger Compartment Doors, Left 840 Subzone - Passenger Compartment Doors, Right

B. Prepare for the Test

SUBTASK 52-71-00-860-002 (1) Make sure that this circuit breaker is closed: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3 Row Col Number Name B 13 C00131 MASTER CAUTION ANNUNCIATOR BAT

C. Test

SUBTASK 52-71-00-860-003 (1) Make sure that the door to be tested is fully closed, latched and locked. SUBTASK 52-71-00-860-005 (2) Make sure the forward airstair door is fully closed, latched and locked. SUBTASK 52-71-00-860-004 WARNING MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT ENGAGE THE GIRT BARS FOR THE ESCAPE SLIDE IN THE FLOOR FITTINGS. YOU MUST DO THIS BEFORE YOU START THE TEST. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THEN THE ESCAPE SYSTEM CAN DEPLOY WHEN YOU OPEN THE DOOR. THIS CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT. (3) For the entry and galley service doors, make sure that the escape slide girt bars are not engaged in the floor fittings. SUBTASK 52-71-00-210-001 (4) Make sure that the applicable door warning light on the Forward Overhead Panel, P5, is off. (a) Make sure that the two MASTER CAUTION lights in the master caution annunciators on the Glareshield Panel, P7, are off. If the lights are on, push the MASTER CAUTION reset. (b) Make sure that the DOORS lamp in the master caution annunciator on the right hand side of the Glareshield Panel, P7, is off. If the lamp is on, push the MASTER CAUTION reset. EFFECTIVITY ALL SUBTASK 52-71-00-730-002 (5) Do this test on the airstair door: NOTE: The airstair door warning system has two sensors. One sensor indicates if the lockpin is retracted and the other sensor indicates if the door is open. The two sensors are connected to the same door warning indication lights in the flight deck. (a) Make sure all the doors are closed. (b) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR CAUTION DO NOT HOLD THE AIRSTAIR CONTROLS IN THE NORMAL EXTEND POSITION FOR MORE THAN 120 SECONDS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THEN DAMAGE TO THE LOCKPIN ACTUATORS CAN OCCUR. CAUTION DO NOT APPLY POWER TO THE AIRSTAIRS CONTROLS FOR MORE THAN 5 CYCLES, ONE AFTER THE OTHER ONE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THEN DAMAGE TO THE LOCKPIN ACTUATORS CAN OCCUR. (c) Put exterior airstair controls in the NORMAL EXTEND position. (d) Make sure the two MASTER CAUTION lights in the master caution annunciators on the Glareshield Panel, P7, come on. (e) Make sure the DOORS lamp in the master caution annunciator on the right hand side of the Glareshield Panel, P7, comes on. (f) Make sure the airstair door warning light on the Forward Overhead Panel, P5, comes on. (g) Release the airstair controls. (h) Make sure the two MASTER CAUTION lights in the master caution annunciators on the Glareshield Panel, P7, go off. (i) Make sure the DOORS lamp in the master caution annunciator on the right hand side of the Glareshield Panel, P7, goes off. (j) Make sure the airstair door warning light on the Forward Overhead Panel, P5, goes off. (k) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR (l) Put the exterior airstair controls in the NORMAL EXTEND position until the airstair door is open. (m) Release the controls. (n) Make sure the two MASTER CAUTION lights in the master caution annunciators on the Glareshield Panel, P7, come on. (o) Make sure the DOORS lamp in the master caution annunciator on the right hand side of the Glareshield Panel, P7, comes on. EFFECTIVITY ALL (p) Make sure the airstair door warning light on the Forward Overhead Panel, P5, comes on. (q) Close the airstair door. (r) Make sure the two MASTER CAUTION lights in the master caution annunciators on the Glareshield Panel, P7, go off. (s) Make sure the DOORS lamp in the master caution annunciator on the right hand side of the Glareshield Panel, P7, goes off. (t) Make sure the airstair door warning light on the Forward Overhead Panel, P5, goes off.

F. Removal of the Entry and Galley Service Door Indication

SUBTASK 52-71-11-020-001 (1) Remove the sensor assembly [1]: (a) For the forward entry door, do these steps: 1) Remove the bolts [23] that attach the cover [6] to the sensor assembly [1]. 2) Remove the bolts [3] and washers [2] that attach the sensor assembly [1] to the latch receiver [7]. 3) For airplanes with sensor assembly P/N 284A1322-1, remove the screws [12], washers [13], and nuts [14] that attach the proximity sensor [11] to the sensor assembly [1]. 4) For airplanes with sensor assembly P/N 284A1322-2, -3, -4, -5, -6, -7, -8, or -9, remove the screws [12], spacers [24], and nuts [14] that attach the proximity sensor [11] to the sensor assembly [1]. 5) Cut the wires that connect the proximity sensor [11] to the airplane wiring as near as possible to the proximity sensor [11]. 6) Remove the proximity sensor [11]. (b) For the aft entry door and aft galley service door, do these steps: 1) Remove the screws [4] and washers [5] that attach the cover [6] to the sensor assembly [1]. 2) Remove the bolts [3] and washers [2] that attach the sensor assembly [1] to the latch receiver [7]. 3) Remove the screw [8], shim [26], and shims [27] that attach the sensor assembly [1] to the fuselage frame. 4) Remove the screws [12], washers [13], and nuts [14] that attach the proximity sensor [11] to the sensor assembly [1]. 5) Cut the wires that connect the proximity sensor [11] to the airplane wiring as near as possible to the proximity sensor [11]. 6) Remove the proximity sensor [11]. (c) For the forward galley service door, do these steps: 1) Remove the screws [4] and washers [5] that attach the cover [6] to the sensor assembly [1]. 2) Remove the bolts [3] and washers [2] that attach the sensor assembly [1] to the latch receiver [7]. 3) Remove the screw [44], washer [45], shim [46], filler [47], washer [48], and nut [49] that attach the sensor assembly [1] to the fuselage frame. 4) Remove the screws [12], washers [13], and nuts [14] that attach the proximity sensor [11] to the sensor assembly [1]. 5) Cut the wires that connect the proximity sensor [11] to the airplane wiring as near as possible to the proximity sensor [11]. 6) Remove the proximity sensor [11].

SUBTASK 52-71-11-420-001 (1) Install the sensor assembly [1]: (a) Identify the correct connections between the sensor assembly wiring and airplane wiring (WDM 52-71-11). NOTE: Make sure the sensor wires are connected to the correct airplane wires. If the wires are not correctly connected the sensor will not operate. G. Adjustment of the Entry and Galley Service Door Indication Sensor

SUBTASK 52-71-11-820-005 (1) To adjust the sensor, do these steps: (a) Get access to the PSEU through this panel: Number Name/Location 112A Forward Access Door (b) Use the Proximity Sensor Electronics Unit (PSEU) Built-In-Test Equipment (BITE) to test the sensor. 1) Push the ON/OFF switch on the PSEU BITE display. 2) Push the down arrow until OTHER FUNCTNS? shows. 3) Push the YES switch to select OTHER FUNCTNS? 4) Push the down arrow until SENSOR RIGGING? shows. 5) Push the YES switch to select SENSOR RIGGING? 6) Push the down arrow until the applicable sensor identification shows. a) Make sure that the correct code is displayed for the applicable door: • S199 is FWD ENTR LKD EFFECTIVITY ALL • S194 is FWD SERV LKD • S200 is AFT ENTR LKD • S195 is AFT SERV LKD 7) Push the YES switch to select the sensor. 8) Push the YES switch to select GAP GRAPH? The sensor number and clearance display meter will show (Figure 203). NOTE: You can also display the clearance value in MILS (1 MIL equals 1/1000th of an inch) or required changes to the sensor clearance. Push on the down arrow or NO switch to show these options. (c) Make sure that the PSEU display shows the sensor clearance (blinking icon) between the solid posts. NOTE: If the sensor clearance is too large for detection the display will show “TGT FAR”. (d) If the sensor clearance is not between the solid posts or TGT FAR is shown, do these steps to adjust the sensor/target clearance: NOTE: Get the sensor clearance as close as possible to the optimum gap clearance by pushing the plunger flush with the surface of the latch receiver when adjusting. The clearance can be different after the PSEU Sensor Rigging test is completed. 1) Determine what adjustment is needed for the correct sensor clearance. a) At the GAP VALUE display, push the down arrow for the Gap Move Value. b) Record the Gap Move Value. NOTE: The Gap Move Value represents the distance in mils the target needs to move toward or away from the sensor face to achieve the optimum gap for that sensor. 2) Open the applicable door. 3) If the cover [6] is installed on the sensor assembly [1], remove the cover [6]: a) Remove the bolts [23] or the screws [4] and washers [5] that attach the cover [6] to the sensor assembly [1]. b) Remove the cover [6] from the sensor assembly [1]. 4) If the sensor clearance is out of tolerance, do these steps: a) Remove lockwire or safety cable from the jam nuts [15]. b) Loosen the jam nuts [15]. c) Use the recorded Gap Move Value to adjust the target position. <1> For the Type 1 sensor assembly [1] (with one jam nut): <a> Turn the slotted end of the plunger [10] to move the target until the clearance is the optimum gap (Table 201). NOTE: The clearance is applicable to the full face of the proximity sensor. <2> For the Type 2 sensor assembly [1] (with two jam nuts): <a> Turn the two jam nuts [15] on the plunger [10] to move the target until the clearance is the optimum gap (Table 201). <3> Make sure that the target is parallel to the proximity sensor [11]. <4> If necessary adjust the target so that it is parallel to the proximity sensor [11]. EFFECTIVITY ALL d) Tighten the jam nuts [15]. e) Close and lock the door. f) Examine the clearance value on the PSEU. g) Repeat the steps to adjust the target and then check the clearance until it is within tolerance of the optimum gap (Table 201). Table 201/52-71-11-993-801 Sensor # Door Optimum Gap Tolerance S199 Fwd Entry 0.1 in. (100.0 mils) +/- 0.02 in. (20.0 mils) S200 Aft Entry 0.1 in. (100.0 mils) +/- 0.02 in. (20.0 mils) S194 Fwd Service 0.16 in. (160.0 mils) +0.02 in. (20.0 mils) / - 0.07 in. (70.0 mils) S195 Aft Service 0.1 in. (100.0 mils) +/- 0.02 in. (20.0 mils) h) Install MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912, or safety cable kit, G51827 (optional), on the jam nuts [15] (PAGEBLOCK 20-10-44/401). (e) Do this task: Entry and Galley Service Door Indication Sensor Test (S194, S195, S199, or S200), TASK 52-71-11-710-801.

10. Forward Entry Door Switch Test (S1147) (Figure 205) NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. General

(1) This procedure is applicable for the S1147 indication switch on the forward entry door. (2) Two mechanics can be necessary to complete this procedure. One mechanic to manually operate the switches and the second mechanic to operate the lights in the flight compartment. (3) For the indication sensors (S194, S195, S199, or S200) on the entry or galley service doors, refer to Entry and Galley Service Door Indication Sensor Test (S194, S195, S199, or S200), TASK 52-71-11-710-801.

B. References

Reference Title 52-11-00-860-803 Open the Door with the Interior Handle (P/B 201)

C. Prepare for the Procedure

SUBTASK 52-71-11-840-002 (1) Prepare for the test: (a) Make sure that all of the doors that show on the Door Warning Panel (P5) are closed and latched. SUBTASK 52-71-11-720-002 (2) The system test: (a) Push the MASTER CAUTION light on the Glareshield (P7). 1) Make sure that the MASTER CAUTION light and the DOORS light go OFF. (b) Open the Main Entry Door. 52-71-61-710-801Forward Airstair Door Lockpin Sensor S282 TestPDF p. 1554

5. Forward Airstair Door Lockpin Sensor S282 Test NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.

A. References

Reference Title 24-22-00-860-811 Supply Electrical Power (P/B 201) 24-22-00-860-812 Remove Electrical Power (P/B 201) 52-61-00-710-802 Airstair Door Operation Without Airstairs Installed (P/B 201) 52-61-00-860-802 Forward Airstair Retraction (P/B 201)

B. Location Zones

Zone Area 117 Electrical and Electronics Compartment - Left

C. Prepare for the Test

SUBTASK 52-71-61-860-001 (1) Supply electrical power to the airplane (TASK 24-22-00-860-811).

D. Forward Airstair Door Lockpin Sensor S282 Test

SUBTASK 52-71-61-730-002 (1) Do this test on the sensor [1]: (a) Make sure the airstair door is closed. 1) If airstair not installed, do this task: Airstair Door Operation Without Airstairs Installed, TASK 52-61-00-710-802 (b) If installed, remove the INOP collar from circuit breakers C00409 and C00411. NOTE: The inoperative circuit breakers should remain open but these circuit breakers can be closed temporarily to complete the test procedure. These circuit breakers should have safety collars which must be re-installed after the airstair door is closed. Close these circuit breakers: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR NOTE: The safety collars must be re-installed on the circuit breakers after this test. (c) Install an INOP placard on the airstair control panel that will not be operated to do this test. CAUTION DO NOT HOLD THE AIRSTAIR CONTROLS IN THE NORMAL EXTEND POSITION FOR MORE THAN 120 SECONDS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY, THEN DAMAGE TO THE LOCKPIN ACTUATORS CAN OCCUR. EFFECTIVITY ALL (CAUTION PRECEDES) CAUTION DO NOT APPLY POWER TO THE CONTROLS FOR MORE THAN 5 CONTINUOUS CYCLES. IF YOU APPLY POWER TO THE ACTUATORS FOR MORE THAN 5 CYCLES, DAMAGE TO THE EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR. (d) Push and hold the EXTEND switch on the interior control panel for five seconds. NOTE: If the airstair is installed, the airstair motor should not operate. (e) Make sure the AIRSTAIR door warning light on the Forward Overhead Panel, P5, comes on. (f) Release the airstair controls. (g) Make sure the airstair door warning light on the Forward Overhead Panel, P5, remains on. (h) Put the interior airstair controls in the RETRACT position until the airstair door is fully closed. 1) Do this task: Forward Airstair Retraction, TASK 52-61-00-860-802.

E. Put the Airplane Back to its Usual Condition

SUBTASK 52-71-61-860-002 (1) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags: F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-4 Row Col Number Name A 16 C00409 FWD AIRSTAIR DOOR C 17 C00411 FWD AIRSTAIR STBY DOOR ACTR SUBTASK 52-71-61-020-002 (2) Remove the INOP placard from the applicable airstair control panel. SUBTASK 52-71-61-860-003 (3) Remove electrical power from the airplane if it not necessary (TASK 24-22-00-860-812).
